Commentary of Ibn ʿAṭiyya (al-Muḥarrar al-Wajīz) on Surah 103, verses 1–3:

(p-685)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

Tafsir of Surat al-ʿAṣr

It is Meccan.

The words of the Exalted and Majestic:

﴿By time﴾ ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ ﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾

Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "al-ʿAṣr" is ad-dahr (time, an age). It is said of it: ʿaṣr and ʿaṣur, with a ḍammah on the ʿayn and the ṣād. Imru' al-Qays said:

"…… and do they cover those who were in the past age?"

Qatādah said: "al-ʿAṣr" is al-ʿashiyy (the late afternoon/evening). Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ about al-ʿAṣr, and he said: 'Your Lord swears by the end of the day.'" Some scholars, and Abū ʿAlī mentioned it, said: al-ʿAṣr is the day, and al-ʿAṣr is the night. From this is the saying of Ḥumayd:

"The two ʿaṣrs will not linger: a day and a night, when they seek to overtake whatever they aim at."

(p-686)Some scholars said: al-ʿAṣr is the early morning (bukrah) and al-ʿAṣr is the evening (ʿashiyyah), and they are the two cool times (al-abradān). Muqātil said: al-ʿAṣr is the Middle Prayer, by which Allah the Exalted swears.

"al-Insān" is a generic noun. "al-Khusr" is deficiency and bad condition. This is entirely clear regarding the disbeliever: that he has lost this world and the Hereafter, and that is the manifest loss. As for the believer, although he is in loss in his worldly life, in his old age and in what he suffers of the hardship of this abode, he is excused in respect of his success in the Hereafter and his profit which does not perish. Whoever, during the span of his life, is engaged in advising one another to truth, patience and acting in accordance with the counsel, there is no loss with him, and he has gathered all good.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: "Wal-ʿaṣr, wa-nawāʾib al-dahr, inna al-insān", and in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: "Wal-ʿaṣr, la-qad khalaqnā al-insān fī khusr." It is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he recited: "Inna al-insān la-fī khusr, wa-innahu fīhi ilā ākhir al-dahr, illā alladhīna", and ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿraj recited: "la-fī khusur" with a ḍammah on the sīn. Salām Abū al-Mundhir recited: "wal-ʿaṣri" with a kasrah on the ṣād, and "wal-ṣabri" with a kasrah on the bāʾ; this is not permissible except in pausal reading (waqf) with transfer of the vowel (naql al-ḥarakah). It is narrated from Abū ʿAmr: "bil-ṣabri" with a kasrah on the bāʾ, an ishmām (partial vowel), and this too occurs only in pausal reading.

The tafsir of Surat [al-ʿAṣr] is complete, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
